Description: Sit down start on a small arête to the right of the overhang pull up on side pulls, finish of on the first bolt of “Kalakazu
Sit down start under the overhang. Nice crossover up to a sloper. Up and over to the bolts of “Kalakazu”
First climb you see as you come up the trail. Intricate moves at the bottom leads to a fine crimp at the top to make the final move over the lip.
This climb, to the left of Kulakaza follows along a 10 ft vertical crack, nice holds, the roof is a little trick.
Take Thor’s hammer and finish up on the anchors of Kalakazu.

Beautiful line on a slightly overhang face, crux 
between first and second bolt with a 2 finger pocket ½ “deep and a shallow scoop 
with a micro flake to crimp a couple surprises awaits you, makes for great 
climbing.
A great start with trick footwork leads to easier climbing above.
Bouldery start leads to nice holds above.
Juggy start leads up to a cool scoop. Use what you can for balance to get up the diagonal ledge.
Starts as for Mosquito Heaven, then traverses left (via a pocketed traverse), and heads to the anchors of Weapons. Fun, if a bit run out.

This excellent route climbs through a series of slopers and pockets up the overhanging right side of the Cedar Wall. The crux is near the top, and involves a LONG reach to a two-finger pocket on a blank slab.
This route deviates from Weapons near the top, stepping left into the positive holds in a shallow dihedral, then traverses right again to the anchors.
This route goes straight up the bolted line and doesn’t go right to the easier side pull. Powerful 2 finger side pulls and gastons leaves you appreciating this fine line.
You’ll know why the name of the route is peachy when you reach the hold above the small roof. This route goes left of the second hangar to a large side pull. Great route.
Great climb with interesting moves, a classic

Start to the right of Tempest on a hard boulder sequence. Traverse right to the overhang on 10b/c moves, up and over the overhang leads to beautiful slots up the top of Calm before the Storm, finish off on Tempests Revenge.
Beautiful climb with great moves on the arête, finish off on the get away biner on Tempest.
Pumpy finish to Calm, hard last clip
an additional hangar added at the top of Tempest and the anchors moved 6 feet higher makes for a difficult crux move but easier last clip
The most difficult route climbed on ninja wall to date. A bouldery start leads to a rest midway. From here, a series of powerful pinches up a 45 degree wall lead to a pocketed finish

Route_Name: Popsicle Pete and the Hurdy Gurdy Girls
Description: A superb short route entirely on pockets-a little bit of Buoux in the north
A nice warm up.
Not as good as it’s neighbour but still worth doing
A tricky climb and not all that popular. Tree anchor.
A nice climb that protects very well. Back stepping off the block to your right at the crux lowers the grade a notch.

Another nice climb with a variety of climbing. Try to avoid using the big flake to the left of the splitter finishing crack. The anchor is set quite far back to force leaders to make the final top out moves. The bolt lower down on the route is intended as a TR directional, not leader protection.
Likely the most popular route at the crag. For TR purposes be sure to put a directional on the upper bolt.
A great route up the face and prow. Has its own anchor on the face at top of prow.
An OK that doesn’t get done often. Shares the anchor (on top of prow) with The Captain
The rats have made this one quite unpleasant. Use caution when topping out on the final block
This route is a second pitch located above Blank Stair/Crystals In My Pocket
Trad with one optional bolt. This route is located approximately 40 m past Magic Carpet Slabs
About 100 m past Magic Carpet Slabs
From the ledge, climb past bolts to the ring anchor. There is a pair of bolts above the ring anchor for setting up a top rope
From the birch tree on the ledge, climb past bolts to the ring anchor
From the ledge, climb past the bolt to the anchor
From the ledge, mantle the small bulge then climb past two bolts to the top
Climb past bolts to the trees at the top. A good route for the beginning leader
Climb over the first ledge, then left up the sickle wall and straight over the roof

Easy climbing on the lower route leads to an excellent face on the upper section. Climb past bolts to the trees at the top. The memorial at the top of this route appeared after the climb was established.
A nice line up a beautiful granite slab. A long sling is useful to sling a flake near the top to avoid running it out.
A sustained, bold lead climbing though the obvious left facing corner to link a series of small seams. Watch for loose rock at 10 m.
Another sustained, bold climb moving left from the left facing corner to climb through another series of thin seams.
A sequential technical testpiece requiring creativity and flexibility to send its sustained crux. Deserves more traffic than it receives.
Unfortunately the dust hasn’t, otherwise this route would be a Giscome classic- well protected and moderately sustained. Approximately 100m west of When the Dust Settles along the road
An excellent introductory gear lead climbs through a crack adjacent to a series of blast holes. Approximately 100m west of When the Dust Settles along the road

Route_Name: Ben’s Brush with the Goddess of Compensation
Description: Sometimes reality nearly mimics television. Named for an eerie coincidence during the first ascent.to a Kids in the Hall skit in which a construction worker wants some paid time off (Compensation!) via a dropped hammer to the head. Approximately 100m west of When the Dust Settles along the road
About 50 m west of Ben’s Brush is this runout, not recommended climb capped by a tottering detached death slab. Approximately 100m west of When the Dust Settles along the road
Layback the left facing corner to right, stepping right at a ledge to climb up the featured face.
Climb the left facing corner into a thin chimney at the top
Starts up right angling finger crack right of the large chimney then pulling through a large layback flake.
Crimp strength and excellent footwork are required on this outstanding route. Stick clip the first bolt as the fall potential from the belay is frightening.
A classic offwidth grovel. Can clip a couple of bolts on the Wild Thing.
The STEEP overhanging Prow is overcome with dynos on good jugs. Blind last clip.
A steep bolted line on the main face. A broken hold at the bouldery crux of this route has increased its difficulty
Fun moves up the right into a left facing layback flake to positive knobs and horns above.
A new route approximately 2m right of Eaglet 3

Giscome Front Bluffs – Right. Small face down and to 
the right of the main bluff. S shaped Finger Crack

Giscome Front Bluffs – Right. Small face down and to 
the right of the main bluff. An OK face climb along the arete

Giscome Front Bluffs – Right. Small face down and to 
the right of the main bluff. This line offers sustained climbing through a series of overlaps. Somewhat difficult to protect.

Giscome Front Bluffs – Right. Small face down and to 
the right of the main bluff. A short 2 bolt sport line requiring a bit of traffic to clean it up

Left branch off the trail up to Eagles' Nest. Easy climbing for most of the route leads into a high crux protected by a bolt. A very small cam (eg. 0.1 X4) is useful after the bolt if you don't like feeling runout. 2 bolt anchor set up to thread for a lower/rappel

Gear: Rack from Camalot 0.3 to 4. Doubles of 3 are ideal.
Description: Corner slightly skiers' right from the anchor (obvious big corner). Nice corner and takes good gear. Traverse right across the flake at the top

Gear: SR of cams and nuts to #1 Camalot.
Description: A committing step onto the face leads to strenuous laybacking through the low crux into a nice corner crack to finish. Directly down the V-shaped gulley from the top anchor.

Stack rocks/reach to the very small holds and pull on. Bouldery moves off the deck lead into a more technical mid-height crux. After the big hold in the middle the climbing mellows out.
Stick clipping/pre-clipping the first bolt is highly recommended.
Hand crack turns to fingers. Traverse right under the roof and pull out onto the arête joining Fledgy's First Flight. Good gear anywhere you want.
Quality face climb with some thin edges and a pumpy finish. Furthest route to the right
Start with your right hand on the positive gaston edge, and your left on a small edge. Reach up to a sloping edge, then a sidepull, and then the top

Start as for Reincarnation, but
power directly left to the arete, and mantle up
Start on the good incut (L) and a sloping crimp (R) at the left edge of the boulder’s overhanging face. Reach up to the sloping edge (R), and throw.
Start as for 2000 Points, but traverse up and right, diagonalling along very small holds, finishing on the final holds of Finger Lickin’. Watch out for the tree!

Start with both hands on the big jug,
reach up left to a sidepull, and use a heel hook to gain the lip. For "The Finger Lickin' Throw" do the same route but dyno it V2.
Simple fun – start on the jugs and climb up.

Start at the extreme right side of the
boulder, and move up on big but sometimes slopey holds
Start as for Gonzo’s Gal, traverse left, and finish on Finger Lickin’.
The backside of the Poultry Boulder is a slab – start below the lip on positive holds, and then climb up the slab
Start low on the positive rail below the lip of the Curry Boulder. Reach up to lip, mantle, and walk up slab.
Start as above, but staying low, traverse right around arete and then uphill on big edges
Start low on slopers on the downhill, right-hand side of the Roadside Boulder. Traverse up and right to big holds, mantle off. No ascents as of this writing.
Start on the positive rail, left of the big jug. Climb straight up on small sloping crimps, using a heel hook. After gaining the lip, and finish by using the hanging boulder left to mantle
Start on big obvious jug, traverse right across sloping shelf, and finish up right around right corner of boulder – stay off the lip before turning the corner
Super low sit-start below the mantle shelf on lie-back crimp. Reach up to shelf and the blocky jug, then reach high and left to a gaston crimp. Reach to lip and mantle. Excellent.
Sit-start using the sloping shelf on the right hand side of the boulder. Move up and a bit right, finish by mantlin
Start as for ATP, but then traverse lip left and finish using the weird mantle on the small hanging boulder.
Start at the left edge of the boulder’s lip, traverse right, and finish by mantling up around the right side of the boulder.
Climb the left-hand face of the Left Arete Boulder, starting on the obvious jug. Good and educational.
Start pinching the arete. Lieback the arete, avoiding the blocky loose rock to your right

Route_Name: The Slow Death of the Right Wing
Description: Climb the right-hand face of the rather loose Right Arete Boulder on edges and sidepulls.
Climb the obvious crack on the right hand face (mostly liebacking)

Harder Variant of Done for the Day. Does not use a heel
hook on the ledge, and mantles directly up at the lip
Mr.Wiggly but dyno it

Start low on good handholds and bad footholds on the left-hand arete of the Crap Boulder. Climb arete, ending on huge horn. (do not topout, but end on jugs at the lip; the rock on the topout is dangerously loose)
Same as Chad's Arete but uses the holds left of the arete. (do not topout, but end on jugs at the lip; the rock on the topout is dangerously loose)

Start as for Chad’s Arete, then move up and right. Finish by reaching left of the finishing holds of Chad’s Arete (do not topout, but end on jugs at the lip; the rock on the topout is dangerously loose)
This powerful traverse starts as for Chad’s Arete, traverses right, and ends on the obvious high jug at the upper right of the boulder.

Start on the low jug in the middle of the boulder.
Reach up to a big hold, and finish on the big hold at the lip. (do not topout, but end on jugs at the lip; the rock on the topout is dangerously loose)

Iron-cross fun. Start on the
jug at the right edge of the boulder, traverse left, and finish on the
final jug of Chad’s. Use only the obvious lower band of holds for the
first half of the problem (do not topout, but end on jugs at the lip; the rock on the topout is dangerously loose)
Start low, sitting down at the left edge of Pat’s Boulder on a big obvious lie-back and a crimp. Move up, and traverse lip to obvious finish at right edge.
Behind Pat’s Boulder is a vertical face. Climb sloping holds to top.
Start down in the hole beneath Wiggling Finger, on the big flake. Traverse a move or two left, then climb up through the little roof. Mats and spotters!
Start left of Reaching For The Sun, on the bad slopers that are used as starting heel hooks on Reaching. Climb straight up – powerful moves.
An area testpiece. Start on low sloper below lip; powerful moves on small holds above and below lip will gain a large sidepull – finish straight up.
. Start as for Reaching, but at large sidepull, continue on lip holds, traversing the lip of the Sun Roof. Superb!
Start at large edge at right side of the Sun Roof. Climb directly up. A low SD start (V2) has also been done.

Start as for Gemini, but traverse down and right. Turn under the lower lip of the boulder to a large sidepull. Climb across underside of boulder, throwing to far lip. Turn lip and toupout directly above.
ssentially the end of Amon Ra – start at lip features and climb directly up
On the end of the Teletubbie Boulder is a giant flake – start on this huge hold and throw to lip
Start on a blunt two-finger undercling (or gaston) and a slopey sidepull at the left end of the alley face of the Front Alley Boulder. Grab these holds, step on, and fire for the top.
A classic. Start quite low on a good, but flat, edge. Move up using thin crimps and creative body english. Mantle off.
Starts on a big flat edge to the right of Group Therapy. Reach to a good crimp, then a slippery gaston, then head for the lip.

Starts low between Put On My Shoe and Fear of Flight on a big edge. Reach up to the little bulge with the good holds, high step, and grab some more good edges on the way to the lip. Not a great landing
. Megaclassic! Starts on the huge flat ledges to the left of The Stooges. Mantle these ledges, and continue up through the bulge on thin holds. Exciting move to the lip!
Starts on the big holds, and climbs up on funky sidepulls and edges. Check out the topout before attempting!
Starts on Ewww, traverses left and finishes on The Stooges.
Starts on the blocky holds, and climbs up to lip on good holds and a funky pod. A tricky mantle to finish.
Starts with a ‘lay-down’ start on a positive blocky hold beneath the lip, and a crimp above the lip. Tricky first move, but the rest is easy

This unusual traverse is a Giscome classic. Start near the middle of the boulder on a very low but good hold in the alcove. Traverse right up the hanging arete (the lower edge of the boulder) on small edges, first by climbing a move or two up the slab, then back down and right. A more direct line (~V10) staying low along the edge has been attempted, but not successfully.
Traverse the wide crack.
Start on the positive edges in the middle of Fall Tsayda Fall, and head straight up. Tricky.
Start on the low, very positive rail/crimp around the corner from Fall Tsyada Fall. A few easy moves lead to the finishing holds of Fall Tsayda Fall.
Climb bottom of the Way of the Warrior then traverse right under roof to the anchor of Weekend Warrior
Chimey the cave by Way of the Warrior then face climb to the anchors
Starts on top of the Dragon Feature
Shares anchors with an open project but the route is climbers right of the anchors
Climb hissy fit to top of crack then angle right along the line of weaknesses ot the anchors of wranglin
Climb to mid bolts of Armageddon Destructor for "Revelations 5.10c"
Runout Traverse
can be climbed as 5.8 to mid anchors
bush rats have infested this climb. 60 M to the climbers right of baby snakes is an obvious right facing corner
immediately right of Dust to Dust

First_Ascent: Lyle Knight, Doug Carter, Joanne Carter, 1988
Lyle Knight, Doug Carter, Joanne Carter, 1988

Description: 1st on the left. Starts in the corner above the scraggly cedar tree. Tree makes for a good belay perch.Start up with easier climbing in the corner and exit up right to the blank feature above.
Middle route. Crimpy crux pulling the overhang. Steep and thin moves get you to the anchor from there.
Right of Wasted Years. For decades it was the only route here. A tricky crux awaits mid way.
Right at the edge of the overhang. Thin moves near the start make for a low crux.

Walk past Wish You Were Here/Shine On for a minute or so, up a hill and you will see the route.  It's marked with a painted sign at the bottom. The name comes from one of our first climbs up this route. Matt was halfway up the wall when a half dozen turkey vultures soared over to check him out and circled overhead for a few minutes. Located just down the wall from Wish You Were Here/Shine On, the route starts with a scramble up to a big ledge. From there, make your way past some tricky slab moves and then move onto the face. Follow the bolt line up from here. About halfway up, you will see two bolts just left of the route in a sort of gully. The recommended route is to stay on the face just to the right of those bolts. Gain the ledge and travel up a short slab to an anchor where nice views await.
Left of Sweet Juniper Stick clip your first bolt and enjoy 5.10 climb with great rests. The crux awaits you at the final bolt - enjoy incredible rock and features, with quality movement.

First route after the large Amphitheatre tapers down to a smaller, 15ish meter wall. Boulder the start to gain a good stance before executing the crux. Sequenced and very committing. Mantle and finish on sustained, but mellower climbing.

This climb is found next to “Sweet, Sweet Juniper.”

The crux is found low on compact limestone. Similar to its neighbour, “Sweet, Sweet Juniper,” the holds are obvious, you get what you get - pull through the crux and the climb gets cruisy.

Gear: Single rack up to a #6. Bolted anchor with rap rings.
Description: Next to “Step Right Up”, the obvious offwidth crack with a visible chockstone.  Scramble up to a ledge before gaining the offwidth crack. Takes good gear.
Starts below the pinnacle on the trail between Revolution Wall and Reborn Wall.

To the right of Step Right Up
Thoughtful corner climb with superb movement exits to cruxy slab with side pulls.

10m right of Step Right Up Fun climb with some reachy moves to good holds. Scramble up to the first ledge, and then make your way up the corner. The arete to the left offers good holds. A brief steep crux leads to a nice ledge for a rest. After the ledge the climb eases. Good holds take you up to the anchor. There are good gear placements along portions of the route if you happen to have your gear rack with you.
Furthest climb on the left. Well-protected face climb on good edges with a tricky start. Shares anchor with Repentless.

Gear: 5 bolts, use last bolt on Face Value. Chain Anchor
Description: Right of Face Value. Slabby with thin edges. Anchor shared with Face Value.
Left of Battle of the Bulge. Well-protected face climb on good edges and pockets with a variety of styles.

Gear: 8 bolts with rap rings at the top. Furthest climb on the right.
Description: Well-protected face climb on good edges.

Gear: SR up to #4 Camalot, chain anchor.
Description: Reborn Wall at the base of the hand line. Start left of the tree and go directly up to ledge. Mantle onto the ledge then up the corner to below the slight overhang. Move to the right, squeezing between the rock and the tree, then up the last steep section. This is the crux and once past it it's an easy scramble to the anchor. The last bit is on moss covered boulders
Right side of big overhang.
Right of High Hopes. An alpine draw will be helpful half way up.
1st bolt line beyond Dark Matter, right next to the trail. Fun moves on good edges over a series of small ledges. Steep 5.7 for the area.
Right of Wish You Were Here. Fun moves lead to the crux exiting the small corner. Shares anchor with Wish You Were Here.
